dataFlow: A shopper on a sold-out product page loads the widget, which checks live availability for the chosen item (product-level or specific variant) and renders a signup form only when it is out of stock; submitting records a waitlist subscription keyed to email + item, deduping repeat signups. When an item restocks, an inventory-change event resolves the affected variant, and the system claims the front of that item's waitlist queue in signup order, emailing as many subscribers as the available units allow (or all, with a limited-stock note), marking each notified once per restock cycle so brief stock dips do not re-blast; remaining subscribers stay queued for the next restock. A scheduler defers any emails that fall inside merchant-configured quiet hours and sends them once the window opens. Each email carries a one-click unsubscribe link that clears the shopper from every waitlist. When a paid order arrives, the system matches its buyer email and purchased items against recently-notified subscriptions to record conversions for the lost-demand-recovered metric. Deleted products clear their waitlists cleanly. The admin dashboard ranks items by waitlist size, drills into subscribers, exports CSV, and edits quiet-hours and notification settings.

edgeCases: A restock inventory webhook is delivered twice for the same item — the second delivery sees availability already in-stock for the open cycle and emails no subscriber a second time.

Only a few units restock while many shoppers wait — notify subscribers in signup order up to the available units, include a limited-stock note in the email, and keep the rest queued for the next restock cycle.
Stock briefly dips to zero and returns within the same restock — because notification is keyed to the restock cycle, no subscriber is re-emailed.
A shopper signs up twice for the same product or variant with the same email — treated as a no-op via the email-plus-item dedup key, while the same email on different items remains separate entries.
A product is deleted while shoppers wait on it — all its waitlist subscriptions are cleared without error, and a deletion for a product with no waitlist is a no-op.
An email send fails for a queued subscriber — leave the subscription unnotified so it is retried on the next notification pass rather than silently lost.
A paid order comes from guest checkout with no matching customer record — conversion matching uses the order's buyer email, so the conversion is still recorded when it matches a notified subscriber.
An inventory change arrives inside quiet hours — the subscriber is marked notify-pending and emailed by the scheduled job once the quiet-hours window opens.
